name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every pending video immediately. This guarantees transcripts exist before any downstream edits or repurposing, cutting rework and speeding delivery. The trade-off is server load—we accept temporary spikes to lock in quality and avoid later scrambles when edits need text.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t server load—it’s that kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript isn’t a stable dependency. If it fails mid-run, we burn time debugging instead of shipping. The better alternative is to use Luma’s built-in transcript tool (from the AI Executive Assistant pattern) for mission-critical work, then validate kimtaeyoon83 only on non-critical backlog. Settle it by running a 10-video pilot with Luma’s tool first—if transcripts are clean, adopt it; if not, fix kimtaeyoon83 before scaling.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the official YouTube API with a quota-backed client to pull transcripts. It’s the only way to guarantee reliability across all videos, not just the ones kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript can handle. The trade-off is upfront setup time for API keys and rate limits, but it eliminates dependency risk and future debugging fires.

name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t just setup time—it’s that a quota-backed YouTube API client turns Operations into a bottleneck. Creatives will still scramble when quotas hit or videos miss transcripts, and the API’s 100-unit daily limit won’t scale for bulk pulls. The better alternative is to run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript in parallel with Luma’s tool, then compare outputs; the mismatch rate settles the argument.

name: Scope
text: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every pending video now. It’s the fastest path to transcripts without waiting for API keys or quota debates. The trade-off is accepting temporary server load spikes, but we lock in immediate progress and avoid downstream scrambles.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t server load—it’s that kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript will fail silently on 10-20% of videos, leaving us with gaps we won’t detect until rework is costly. The better alternative is to use Luma’s built-in transcript tool (from the AI Executive Assistant pattern) for mission-critical runs, then fall back to the YouTube API for the rest. Settle it by running a 10-video pilot: compare transcript success rates between both methods.
